Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www. diOgov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 27 FEB ATTY. BENJIE Y. BAGUIO Vice-Mayor Municipality of Kapatagan Province of Lanao Del Norte Dear Vice-Mayor Baguio: This has reference to your letter requesting for this Department's opinion on "whether or not the local sanggunian can invite the water district especially if the invitation relates to the financial position of the water district in view of the proposed memorandum of agreement (sic) will enter into with the local government unit in the future since our participation extends only to the power to appoint members of the board of directors You stated that the OIC-GeneraI Manager of the local water district manifested that the Sangguniang Bayan cannot invite the water district since it is a form of interference and a form of control or supervision invoking DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2005-21 , dated March 4, 2005 which laid down the Department's position on the operational autonomy of local water districts. You, however, manifested your disagreement to this proposition. Nonetheless, you raised the point that per DILG Memorandum Circular 97-78, dated April 14, 1997, the participation of the municipality in the affairs of the local water district extends only to the power to appoint members of the Board of directors. At the outset, may we point out that the two DILG Circulars abovementioned do not bear substantial significance in resolving your query. Instead, may we stress that the sanggunian, in the discharge of its powers and functions as the local legislative body of the municipality, can invite any person to appear before it to act as resource persons on matters pending before the sanggunian and to provide its members with necessary information which may guide them in coming up with certain measures. May we note, however, that the invitation for one to appear is one thing, and whether the sanggunian can compel the appearance before it of the person so invited is another. In the case of Negros Oriental Electric Cooperative vs. Sangguniang Panlungsod of Dumaguete City, G.R. No. 72492, dated 05 November 1987, the Supreme Court ruled that the Sanggunian, in the exercise of its legislative functions, cannot compel the attendance of any person before it as it is bereft of any statutory power to issue subpoena in the discharge of such functions.

A distinction should, however, be made if the sanggunian is exercising its power to take cognizance of administrative cases filed before it pursuant to Section 61 (b)(c) of the Local Government Code. We refer to this as quasi-judicial power and function of the sanggunian. It bears stressing that per Section 65 of the Local Government Code, the sanggunian is empowered to issue subpoena or compulsory process hence, in this capacity, sanggunian may compel appearance of person before it. The sanggunian however is not left without any other alternative on this. May we note that the invitation was supposed to be in connection with the proposed Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) which the municipality intends to enter into with the local water district. Along this line, you may invite the mayor or for the latter to send his representative to appear before the sanggunian in order to provide the sanggunian with the necessary information relevant to the issue on whether the sanggunian should support the execution of the MOA. This is in line with the duty of the mayor pursuant to Section 444(B)(I )(IV) of the Local Government Code which mandates the mayor to provide the sanggunian with necessary information whenever so required or requested by the said body. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVE C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO Ill Undersecretary Copy Furnished: ARNEL M AGABE, CESO IV Regional Director DILG Region 10
